title: Approvals and sign-offs
before:
1. Submit all stocktake results to the warehouse manager for sign-off.
Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Shift supervisors coordinate counters and recounts on the floor, stock controllers prepare adjustments for review, but neither role may close the count. Withhold system posting until written sign-off is recorded.

2. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager.
Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Attach photographs, WMS records and the inspection note to the request. Do not scrap, discount or adjust stock before approval is granted.

3. Obtain shift-supervisor approval for damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.
The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. Present the damaged stock, value calculation and proposed action during the shift. Record the decision, approver name and time in the damage log before moving goods to quarantine or scrap.

4. Route every inspected return through the shift supervisor for disposition.
The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap after inspection in Zone F. Release restock to Zone B or Zone C, rework to the value-added services area, or scrap only after the disposition is signed.

5. Request overtime exclusively from the warehouse manager.
Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Shift supervisors forecast workload, identify shortfalls in picking, receiving or dispatch, and submit hours, dates and reasons in advance. Do not work additional hours until approval is confirmed and rostered.

6. Book all dock activity through the dispatcher.
The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers under PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Carriers receive a numbered door and scheduled window before arrival. Inbound operators and dispatchers sequence unloading and loading to that plan and report conflicts back to the dispatcher for reallocation.

7. Forward each incident report to the shift supervisor for review.
The shift supervisor reviews every incident report, covering safety events, near misses, equipment damage and operational failures. Initiate the report immediately after making the area safe and notifying supervision. Implement corrective actions only as directed in the review and retain the closed report on file.

8. Nominate new forklift operators solely to the warehouse manager for authorisation.
Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Candidates complete training, assessment and licence verification before nomination. Prohibit solo operation of forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks until written authorisation is issued.

title: Adjustments and racking
before:
1. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments across all storage locations.
2. Complete a second count before any stock adjustment is posted under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
3. Never post an adjustment on a first count alone, even when the variance appears obvious from system stock or pick-face availability.
4. Record the approved recount result as the basis for the adjustment, retaining both count quantities in the system history for audit.
5. Route every adjustment arising from damage through PR-09 Damaged-goods handling before posting it against inventory.
6. Segregate the affected stock physically and systematically while the PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment is completed.
7. Obtain approval for the damaged-goods write-off before posting the corresponding stock adjustment.
8. Submit write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval and posting authority.
9. Escalate write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval, since that threshold requires higher authority.
10. Do not split a single damage event into smaller values to remain below the approval threshold.
11. Verify racking condition during every count round, noting upright impacts, beam deflection, missing pins and load distribution.
12. Respect the limit of 2,700 kg for each rack bay when confirming quantities during recounts and adjustments.

Adjustments must correct the system to verified physical reality, not to expected levels. Where recounts confirm overstock against pallets stored above bay limits, redistribute the load before posting the adjustment.

13. Report any damaged or overloaded bay found during counting to the maintenance technician at once and block that bay from further use.
14. Ensure the maintenance technician maintains racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs arising from count findings.
15. Support the documented racking safety inspection every month by making locations accessible and highlighting suspect bays.
16. Do not use the monthly inspection as a substitute for immediate reporting between inspections; escalate defects on discovery.
17. Hold unresolved adjustment items open to the next count cycle where recount evidence remains inconclusive, rather than forcing the balance.
18. Confirm that approved adjustments are reflected in the system before releasing affected locations back to put-away or picking.

title: Damaged goods
before:
1. Apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling to every crushed carton, leaking unit, collapsed pallet, water-affected pack and suspected contamination found on receipt, in storage, at picking or on return.
2. Move the affected stock to the quarantine area in Zone F on the same shift it is found, keeping pallet integrity and labels intact for assessment.
3. Record the date, location found, product code, quantity, damage type, photographs where required, and the discovering operator in the system quarantine record.
4. Segregate damaged units from saleable stock inside quarantine, preventing any put-away, replenishment, picking or dispatch until assessment is complete.
5. Assign assessment without delay to trained personnel on the shift, preserving cold-chain or hazmat controls during the transfer where applicable.
6. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap, completing that inspection BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision is taken.
7. Assess all other damaged goods on the same basis: confirm quantity and condition first, then recommend restock to saleable locations, rework in the designated area, or scrap with stated reason.
8. Obtain written write-off approval before scrapping or adjusting any value from inventory, attaching the assessment and supporting evidence to the request.
9. Send write-offs valued up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval, providing the quarantine reference, quantities and calculated value.
10. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval, since damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval and must not proceed on lower authority.
11. Confirm that the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR and the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR, routing each case strictly by its total value.
12. Post the approved disposition on the same day wherever the shift allows: release restock to its system-directed location, transfer rework to its holding position, and remove scrapped units through the authorised scrap route.
13. Retain the quarantine record, assessment, approval and system adjustment together for audit, linking the stock adjustment to the PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment that authorised it.
14. Review open quarantine positions at each shift handover, carrying unresolved assessments forward with named owner and required completion time until closure.

title: Spills, Quarantine and Damaged Goods
before:
1. Stop work in the affected area immediately when you discover a leak, spill or damaged container. Warn nearby personnel, eliminate ignition sources where safe to do so, and prevent the substance spreading to aisles, drains or other zones.

2. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every chemical, fuel, battery-acid or unidentified liquid spill. Follow the spill-kit instructions for containment and absorption, wear the specified protective equipment, and ventilate the area as directed.

3. Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Do not attempt clean-up beyond your training; wait for instruction and handover control of the scene on arrival.

4. Segregate all suspect, leaking, temperature-affected or damaged stock at once. Move affected pallets and cartons to quarantine, using clean handling equipment to avoid cross-contamination.

5. Place all quarantined stock only in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not leave quarantined goods in receiving, bulk storage, picking or dispatch aisles, on dock approaches or in pedestrian walkways.

6. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep quarantine, inspection, rework and value-added tasks physically separated within Zone F. Maintain clear access to the quarantine area for inspection and removal at all times.

7. Returns are inspected in Zone F. Transfer inbound returns directly to the inspection point and hold them there until disposition is decided. Do not restock, rework or scrap any return before inspection is complete.

8. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Record the inspection result, quantity, condition and proposed disposition in the system and attach the disposition label to each unit.

9. Execute PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for every damaged, crushed, punctured, wet or contaminated unit found on receipt, in storage, during picking or on return. Photograph the damage, retain packaging and labels where safe, and enter the full quantity and value in the damage record.

10. Obtain write-off approval before scrapping or adjusting any damaged stock. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

11. Apply the approval threshold to each damage event separately. Do not divide one event to remain within a lower limit. Escalate any dispute over value or responsibility to the shift supervisor for decision.

12. Release quarantined stock only on written authorisation in the system. Return cleared goods to their directed location, send approved rework to the designated position, and dispatch scrap through the controlled route. Review every spill and damage event at shift handover and close all open quarantine records before the next shift starts.

title: Warehouse Manager
before:
The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. The role directs all activity across the warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2, with 2,400 high-bay pallet positions and 8 dock doors.

1. Own site operations across PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, PR-04 Order picking, PR-05 Packing and labelling, PR-06 Outbound dispatch, PR-07 Returns handling, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, PR-12 Cold-chain handling, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, PR-14 Emergency evacuation and PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
2. Lead the direct reporting line for the shift, technical and inventory functions. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
3. Direct inbound, handling and value-added teams through their defined duties. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
4. Maintain operating hours across Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
5. Enforce traffic and storage limits on every shift. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
6. Control racking, unit weight and outbound flow. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 324 full-weight pallets per shift.
7. Account for temperature-controlled and hazardous stock. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and must stay at or below +8 °C. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
8. Act as final sign-off for inventory assurance. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. A full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule.
9. Govern loss and exception decisions. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery.
10. Authorise safety-critical personnel and equipment use. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
11. Oversee rostering, dispatch coordination and incident governance. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. An evacuation drill runs every quarter.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
before:
1. Under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, Harborwick 3PL Ltd. segregates all damaged, suspect and non-conforming stock on the day of discovery and holds it exclusively in the quarantine area in Zone F pending assessment and disposition.

2. Inside Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, quarantine stock remains physically separated from saleable inventory, from value-added work and from all other Zone F holdings until formally released through PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

3. Upon identification, floor staff transfer the affected pallet, carton or unit to quarantine without further put-away, picking or dispatch, while system records retain the original location, quantity and reason for holding until assessment is complete.

4. Assessment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling determines restock, rework or scrap for each quarantine line, with photographic evidence, quantity, value and cause retained against the client stock record.

5. For financial control, Harborwick 3PL Ltd. applies a write-off threshold of 500 EUR per damage event as a firm client commitment.

6. Within that control, the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.

7. Above that threshold, damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and only the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, may authorise the higher-value adjustment.

8. To support transparency, the shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising from damage events, including cause, handling and corrective action, and quarantine status forms part of daily operational reporting.

9. No quarantined goods return to saleable stock, transfer to rework or leave the site as scrap without documented PR-09 Damaged-goods handling assessment and the applicable write-off approval under items 6 and 7.

10. At month end, Harborwick 3PL Ltd. reconciles all quarantine holdings in Zone F against incident reports and write-off approvals, ensuring open quarantine lines, approved disposals and pending decisions are fully visible in client reporting.

11. Through this quarantine discipline, prompt same-day segregation and tiered financial approval, clients receive assured protection of inventory integrity, clear accountability for loss and consistent application of PR-09 Damaged-goods handling across all shifts.
